entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Meryatum was an ancient Egyptian prince and High Priest of Re, son of Pharaoh Ramesses II and Queen Nefertari.

Born during the reign of his father, Meryatum rose to prominence under the rule of Pharaoh Ramses III (1186–1155 BCE), succeeding his brother as High Priest of Re.

As High Priest, Meryatum oversaw the construction of several temples and monuments, including the Temple of Re at Avaris.

Meryatum's significance lies in his role as a symbol of royal authority and priestly power during this period of ancient Egyptian history.

His legacy is marked by the enduring influence of the Temple of Re on subsequent architectural and religious developments in Egypt.

A notable quote from the Greek historian Herodotus (c. 484 – c. 425 BCE) reflects Meryatum's importance: 'The priests, who are the guardians of the gods, maintain their power through the favor of their rulers.'
